documents.text: During my stay in this apartment, I joined work calls before sunrise, around five in the morning. Audio and video stayed connected.
The building gateway is rebooted before sunrise at five each morning. My work calls from the apartment lost their connection at that time.
I used this unit for online work meetings after dinner, between seven and nine in the evening, without disconnections.
In this apartment the internet became congested after dinner. My evening video calls froze repeatedly.
I tried several brief fifteen-minute video calls from this rental. They stayed connected, but I have no experience with longer sessions here.
The wireless connection in the rental dropped twice during a fifteen-minute call with my team.
I completed a continuous six-hour remote training session from the apartment with working audio and video throughout.
A session timeout on this property's connection disconnects my video meeting after three hours; short meetings finish normally.
I stayed in the bedroom on Saturday and Sunday and heard no neighboring celebrations while sleeping.
On Saturday and Sunday nights, celebrations next door kept me awake in this apartment. The noise continued past midnight.
During my Monday-through-Thursday stay the apartment bedroom was quiet overnight. I was not there on the weekend.
A neighboring loading dock woke me in this apartment before dawn every Monday through Thursday. I have no weekend observations.
This apartment advertises internet, Wi-Fi and a desk. The advertisement gives no call reliability, duration or time-of-day observations.
The apartment is near a conference center whose evening program includes quiet study hours. This is not information about the rental's network or sound insulation.
My internet connection in this apartment was unreliable during video meetings. I did not record the time or the length of the calls.
On a weekday before sunrise, traffic noise in this bedroom disrupted my video meeting even though the connection stayed up.
After dinner on Saturday, loud music from the next unit interrupted my work call in this apartment; the network itself remained connected.
The landlord describes the apartment as quiet. No resident observations or time-specific details are supplied.

cases.query: I need a rental for reliable video meetings before sunrise at five in the morning.
I need a rental for reliable video meetings after dinner between seven and nine in the evening.
My remote team check-ins last fifteen minutes. I need a reliable video connection in the rental.
I attend uninterrupted six-hour remote training sessions and need the rental connection to keep audio and video working.
I sleep in the apartment on Saturday and Sunday nights and want quiet surroundings.
I sleep in the apartment Monday through Thursday and want quiet surroundings before dawn.
On weekdays before sunrise I need reliable video meetings and a quiet room in the rental.
On Saturday evenings after dinner I need reliable video meetings and a quiet room in the rental.

label_notes: Scenario-relevant includes explicit evidence about a requested context dimension or an explicit observation limit for that dimension. Weekday sources explicitly say weekends were not observed, so they inform the weekend evidence gap. Brief-ok explicitly says longer sessions were not tested. Extended-risk describes both short-session normal operation and long-session failure. Early-weekday/evening-weekend report connected network plus noise: they are relevant to network cases but count as risk only when quiet is requested. Generic network risk is topic-relevant but lacks context specificity, so excluded from scenario labels; this is not a claim it should be hidden from the actual user. Multi-topic labels are a union of relevant context dimensions, not proof of meeting every constraint.
